headline: Fortune reports that Nvidia chief Jensen Huang has become the loudest critic of AI doom warnings, while Nvidia launched a new system to stop AI agents from going rogue.
score_reason: Read in full; a roundup of Huang's earlier remarks plus one new Nvidia product, so only part of it is fresh.
importance_line: It shows industry leaders openly split on AI risk, which shapes how governments set rules, but Fortune itself notes that fast AI and agent-safety products both help Nvidia sell chips.
summary: Fortune reports that Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has repeatedly rejected warnings that AI threatens humanity, telling CBS News about two weeks ago that other AI leaders such as OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei were "irresponsible" for the "doomsday narratives" in their recent reports. Fortune adds that Nvidia has launched its Open Agent Safety Platform to keep AI agents inside the limits they are given, and notes that faster AI development also helps Nvidia sell more chips.
notes: REPLY ELEMENT: Huang answers warnings from Altman and Amodei (the article gives no dates or titles for the reports he means, so none is named). The Nvidia launch is dated 'Monday' in the text of a 4 Oct article; the date is as printed by Fortune.
